","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Honouring the Life and Service of Bob Brown OAM
 
Today, we pause to honour the life and legacy of Bob Brown OAM, a man whose dedication to our community has left an enduring mark on the Berrigan Shire.
Bob served the Berrigan Shire Council for many years as a committed volunteer, offering his time, his wisdom and his unwavering passion for preserving our local aviation history. As President of the Tocumwal Historic Aerodrome Museum, Bob played a pivotal role in safeguarding one of the most significant collections of World War II and Tocumwal aviation artefacts in Australia. 
 
He was instrumental in the initiation of the Tocumwal Aviation Museum.  His work ensured that future generations will continue to learn from and appreciate the stories, sacrifices and achievements that shaped our region. 
 
On behalf of Council, I extend our heartfelt condolences to Bob’s wife Gina and to his extended family. His legacy will continue to inspire all who value aviation history, community and service.

 










RESOLVED OCM-14-2026 

Moved: Mayor McKean

That Council Officers prepare a submission to the Minister of Local Government before 31 March 2026 in accordance with the following direction:
 
  1. Notes the perceived value of being a member of a Joint Organisation outlined in the Riverina and Murray Joint Organisation paper on this matter. 
 
  1. Resolves the following provisions be reviewed for exclusion from the Joint Organisation Statutory obligations and form the basis of the Berrigan Shire submission
        a. The requirement for a member funded Audit Risk and Improvement Committee be abolished, or be funded by the NSW State Government.
        b. The requirement for audited Annual accounts be abolished, or funded by the NSW state Government.
        c. Objection to the requirements of the Code of Meeting Practice that prevents remote attendance on the grounds that such conditions may be discriminatory in both form and practice.
        d. The compliance costs for smaller regional councils and Joint Organisations are excessive to meet in a rate capped environment.

    3. Notes the attachments provided by the CEO in consideration of this matter, the RAMJO charter, the RAMJO comparative analysis, the minister's letter and the RAMJO presentation on the value of Joint Organisations.

         4. Reserves the right to reconsider the current membership of RAMJO, including whether a ROC would be a better option, when the review is tabled.

  1. Notes previous Council resolutions item 9.3 Notice of Motion - Berrigan Water Tower Mural OCM171/25 Oct 2025 and financial contributions totaling $13,000 toward the Berrigan Water Tower Art Project.
  2. Notes that a letter of support was provided to the Berrigan Tidy Towns and Conservation Group to assist with their grant applications for the project.
  3. Notes that Council has worked collaboratively with the Berrigan Tidy Towns and Conservation Group regarding fencing and electricity supply requirements for the project site.
  4.   5. Request that the Berrigan Tidy Towns and Conservation Group provide a detailed strategic plan of proposed works and staging, including costings and demonstrated community endorsement, and that council will consider additional funding or seeking grant opportunities.

Carried

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"My question relates to the ongoing dog issues in Kelly Street, Tocumwal.  Residents have raised concerns there is a long term issue in this area.  Can officers please provide to Council:
 
Question -  summary of the current legislative options for dealing with dog issues.
Answer- Depending on the nature of the complaint, officers may inspect the site and discuss the matter with the dog owner(s). Council officers will follow up these discussions in writing, where appropriate. If the complaint continues, officers may again speak with the owner(s) and issue a formal warning. Where ongoing non‑compliance is identified and officers are required to undertake further follow‑up, a penalty notice may be issued. Any issued fine is payable to Revenue NSW. Where a matter is of a serious nature, such as a dog attack, Council officers may take immediate enforcement action, including the issuing of a penalty notice, once relevant evidence has been provided and reviewed. Council has not previously had a Companion Animals related Local Order for Berrigan Shire (that is, additional controls beyond the requirements of the Act). Officers are currently working toward the development of a proposed Local Order, which will be subject to the statutory process under the Local Government Act 1993.


Question - A summary of the issues raised over the years in Kelly Street=
Answer - Council officers received multiple telephone complaints from an adjoining landowner regarding alleged dog barking at the subject property in September 2024, and again in June and July 2025. In September 2024, a Council officer attended the location and parked outside the property for approximately 30 minutes to observe the alleged nuisance. During this inspection, no dog barking was heard. In June 2025, officers attended the property and spoke with the dog owner regarding the complaint. During this interaction, the owner became abusive towards officers. Officers nevertheless advised the owner of their responsibilities and obligations under the Companion Animals Act 1998. In July 2025, Council officers issued a formal warning to the owner. The warning outlined that, should the matter continue, the complaint could be progressed as a nuisance dog matter, and that Council may issue a formal order under the Act if warranted.

Question - The actions Council officers have taken in this matter.
Answer -  Outlined previously. Officers have issued a warning. Since the times mentioned above, there have been no other formal complaints.

Question - An update on the current local order process.
Answer - Council officers have drafted a proposed policy and associated Local Order, which are currently under review. Officers have also mapped the required process for introducing the Local Order in accordance with legislative and governance requirements and are seeking to discuss the matter at an upcoming Council workshop.

Question - Options for the fast tracking of the local order process to bring this into law, expediently.
Answer - There is no mechanism available to Council to fast‑track the introduction of a Local Order. The making of Local Orders is prescribed and regulated under the Local Government Act 1993 and must follow the full statutory process, including public exhibition and consideration of submissions. It is also noted that a Local Order cannot be used to control or impose additional or alternative requirements in relation to barking dogs. Matters relating to dog barking and nuisance behaviour are regulated under the Companion Animals Act 1998. Local Orders are limited in scope and are generally directed toward matters such as the keeping and number of animals on premises, and other prescribed issues, including abandoned vehicles and similar property-related controls, rather than behavioural nuisances.","isPublic":false,"isPublished":false,"isCurrentItem":false,"meeting":null,"reports":[{"id":144,"name":"Report","isUploaded":0,"reportTemplateId":1,"wordTemplateId":2,"pdfMediaFullPath":"stream/BERRIGANSHIRE/tmp_0c00fa8a8e.pdf","token":"eebc6f19-5e68-41b5-8d12-64dd67a68a8c","isPublic":false}],"attachments":[],"actionSheets":[],"bookmarks":[{"id":62,"name":"26","eventId":10,"title":"Question with Notice - Cr John Stringer\u00A0","text":"Question with Notice - Cr John Stringer\u00A0","startTime":3228,"duration":null,"itemId":633,"sortOrder":27,"minutesSortOrder":27,"parentId":-1,"additionalParentId":-1}],"minutes":[{"id":139,"motionedByName":null,"secondedByName":null,"motionAction":null,"voteForNames":null,"voteAgainstNames":null,"voteAbstainNames":null,"voteResult":null,"motionText":""}]},{"id":632,"name":"Question with Notice - Mayor Julia Cornwell McKean ","parentId":361,"sortOrder":34,"minutesSortOrder":35,"minutesParentId":361,"outlineNumber":"2.","fullOutlineNumber":"11.2.","htmlContent":"

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Please find below the answer to the question regarding vandalism and CCTV cameras as per agenda item 11.2:
 
At time of writing, Berrigan Shire Council has published two social media posts about vandalism in the past few weeks.  Can the following information please be provided:

Question - please advise, with specifics, what vandalism and related crimes (eg theft) have occurred at Tocumwal playgrounds and when it is believed to have occurred.
Answer - An incident occurred at the Tocumwal Foreshore Playground on or around 3 April whereby an item of playground equipment was found damaged and located on site. The item has been identified and arrangements are in place for replacement. The incident is believed to be vandalism however no offender has been identified or charged as of yet. A formal report has been made to Police. No further incidents have occurred since January 2026. 

Question - please advise, with specifics, what vandalism and related crimes have occurred at the Barooga Botanical gardens and when it is believed to have occurred. 
Answer - On Easter weekend there were reports of minor damage and potential antisocial behavior without any formal complaints received. Such incidents are recorded through BSC operational reports without escalation to formal incident reports.

Question - please provide details of all property damage, including possible vandalism, and any related crimes (eg theft) that have occurred in Berrigan shire facilities since 1 January 2026
Answer -  Reported incidents include:
 
  • 13 February 2026 a hose used for cleaning toilet cassettes was deliberately cut at the Barooga Dump Point. Item has been replaced with no formal incident recorded.
  • 4 March 2026 a toilet seat was removed and a door lock damaged at Berrigan Hayes Park (Roadside Toilet). N o formal incident reported.

Question - please provide a description of all matters, including property damage and theft, that have been reported to police since 1 January 2026 and the status of each matter.
Answer-  According to NSW Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research (BOSCAR), there are 500-550 total recorded offences per annum across the BSC LGA with the main categories being theft, malicious damage, drug offences and offences against justice procedures. Overall the crime levels in BSC are stated as low to moderate by comparison with NSW regional standards. BOSCAR statistics are only publishes by LGA annually therefore the most recent data available to BSC is from January to December 2025.

Question - In addition there is an unresolved council resolution relating to CCTV and crime statistics in Berrigan Shire.  Please provide an update on what action has been taken to acquit this resolution and when it will be complete.
Answer-   Council passed the following resolution at its October 2025 meeting:


 
That:
1.    That Council receive and note the CCTV Cameras in Public Areas report for September 2025 in response to the Council motion of July 2025 and the retirement of previous outstanding resolutions on this matter.
2.    Receive a report to the November 2025 Council meeting on the current status and issues in relation to the installation and management of CCTV cameras at Council facilities by s355 Committees
3.    Officers undertake a review of the CCTV Surveillance Policy, and the report is to be provided to the February 2026 meeting of Council
4.    $40000 to the 2026/27 Annual Budget for consideration for the implementation of 8 CCTV cameras and associated infrastructure and maintenance.
5.    A Plan on A Page (POAP) to be developed
6.    Implementation of a register to include all damage and theft be created immediately relating to the 8 proposed CCTV sights
7.    All thefts and damage are to be reported to the Police immediately.
 
Council has installed a number of CCTV at council facilities including the Finley Showgrounds (13 cameras and network setup, cost $11,000) and Tocumwal Airport (4 cameras, cost $4,000) Council has investigated the further installation and monitoring of CCTV at other council facilities including evaluating monitored/unmonitored systems, redeployment of existing cameras, data management options and potential use of dummy cameras. Council has further provided consent to S355 Committees to install and maintain their own CCTV systems at applicable facilities. Further evaluation continues on the use of CCTV as it relates to compliance with council-wide policies and legislative obligations, privacy and data management/retention responsibilities and technical support and risk ownership. This will be conducted as part of the broader council policy review and specifically related to the CCTV policy.  The policy review and final acquittal will be completed by FYE 2026.

RED FLEET Update - NSW Government takes responsibility

 

Dear Cr Cornwell McKean,

 

I’m delighted to share with you the very welcome news that from 1 July 2027, the NSW Government will take control of the ownership and management of the Rural Fire Service’s mobile assets – commonly referred to as the “Red Fleet”.

 

For too long councils have been required to record these assets in their financial statements and absorb the depreciation expenses as well as the costs of inspecting and recording these assets in their accounts.

 

Today’s announcement means that once the transfer takes place next year, councils will no longer carry this impost.

 

This is a major win for local government and comes after years of persistent advocacy by LGNSW and from many of you as individual councils.

 

Most recently, our sector made strong representations to the inquiry conducted by the NSW Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee whose final report recommended that legal ownership of the fleet should be transferred to the RFS as a state agency.

 

We are pleased that the State Government has acted so decisively on this key recommendation to transfer ownership.

 

Councils have always supported the work of the RFS and recognise that it is a world leading firefighting service.

 

We now look forward to working with the State Government over the next 12 months to ensure a successful transition, including appropriate consideration of maintenance contracts.

 

Please find below the full media statement from Minister Dib and Minister Hoenig released this morning.

 

 

Yours sincerely,

 

 

Mayor Darcy Byrne

President, LGNSW

 

 

 

 

 

MEDIA RELEASE: Investing in regional jobs and RFS fleet management

Friday, 12 June 2026

 

The Minns Labor Government is backing regional communities with a $470 million investment in the 2026-27 NSW Budget to modernise management of the NSW Rural Fire Service (RFS) fleet.

 

This 10-year commitment is about enhancing bush fire and emergency response to better protect communities in our regions by ensuring RFS trucks are safe and reliable.

 

More than $29 million will be invested over two years to establish up to eight RFS regional maintenance hubs and providers, along with $106 million over four years for critical maintenance and safety upgrades.

 

These hubs will be job and apprenticeship creators for regional communities, supporting local industry and strengthening the resilience of the RFS into the future.

 

The Minns Labor Government will also introduce legislation to transfer ownership of the States ‘red fleet’ of more than 6,000 firefighting vehicles from councils to the RFS.

 

This reform will consolidate operational responsibility for the red fleet under the State Government for the first time since the RFS was established almost 30 years ago. Ownership and management would be transferred from councils from 1 July 2027.

 

The new arrangements will deliver consistent statewide standards and improved reliability and vehicle lifecycle management, better reflecting the current operating model while continuing the longstanding partnership with councils to support emergency services.

 

Councils will be engaged over the coming twelve months to support the transition and identify opportunities to assist with future maintenance.

 

Emergency Services Minister Jihad Dib and Local Government Minister Ron Hoenig today joined Member for Leppington Nathan Hagarty and RFS Commissioner Trent Curtin to visit the new Catherine Field Brigade fire station and inspect vehicles that will be part of the fleet transition.

 

More than $34.5 million has been invested to upgrade 28 rural fire brigade stations and Fire Control Centres this financial year, out of a wider $716.4 million investment in the RFS.

 

Emergency Services Minister Jihad Dib said:

“We are planning for the future and investing in our firefighting fleet and facilities to strengthen community safety and the resilience of our emergency response. This reform is the next step in making our frontline services fit for the future, giving local communities and our RFS volunteers the support they need to respond to bush fires and other emergencies.

 

“Our focus on the state’s firefighting capability reflects our deep respect for the people who step up when it matters most.

 

“By working with local government to establish new fleet maintenance hubs and services we are also supporting local jobs and industry and ensuring communities benefit from this investment.”

 

 

Minister for Local Government Ron Hoenig said:

“Local councils have made it clear that the existing arrangements no longer reflect the practical reality that the Rural Fire Service operates the fleet, while councils continue to carry ownership and accounting responsibilities.

 

“Before any decision was made, it was important to understand how these arrangements arose, the role local government had historically sought to retain, and the consequences of any change.

 

“The Government has now accepted a pathway that aligns ownership with operational responsibility while recognising the continuing and important role councils play in bushfire prevention, hazard reduction and emergency management.

 

“Councils remain valued partners in protecting their communities, and this reform provides greater clarity about responsibilities while reducing an administrative burden that councils have consistently raised.”

 

 

RFS Commissioner, Trent Curtin said:

“This is a landmark and momentous reform for the RFS and one of the most significant investments in our operational capability in recent years.

 

“Our firefighters rely on these vehicles every day in some of the most demanding and unpredictable conditions, and it is essential we equip them with a fleet that is safe, reliable and fit for purpose.

 

“This reform establishes, for the first time, a consistent and modern approach to fleet management across NSW. It strengthens safety, improves reliability and ensures our members are always ready to respond when communities need them most.

 

 

Local Government NSW President Darcy Byrne said:

“Having the red fleet off the balance sheets of local councils is a big win for local government.

 

“Many councils that are struggling to overcome financial constraints will be relieved to have this problem resolved.

 

“We look forward to working with the Government to ensure a successful transition over the next 12 months.”

 

 

Country Mayors Association Chairman Rick Firman said:

"The Country Mayors Association NSW Board and our 89 Rural, Remote & Regional Council Members welcome the Government’s decision.

 

“We have worked hard with the Government to remove the RFS assets from our books to reflect the current reality that these assets are operated by the RFS, not Councils.

 

“Minister Dib as well as the Treasurer have both always made time to meet with us to discuss this most important issue. They realise that we need strong Councils in the bush, and this decision will go some way to assisting with our critical issue of financial sustainability.”

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"RESOLVED OCM-142-2026 

Moved: Mayor Cornwell McKean
Seconded: Councillor Dennis
That Council:
  1. Welcomes the Federal Government’s recent announcement recognising the very real challenge of financial sustainability impacting the Local Government sector and committing to a meaningful, ongoing, annual increases in the level of Financial Assistance Grants;
  2. Welcomes the announcement of the Federation Compact with Local Government that commits to:
      1. Ongoing annual increases to Financial Assistance Grants to return them to historic levels;
      2. Ensure Roads to Recovery funding can be used to purchase plant and equipment to enable councils to carry out their own road maintenance with their own trained workers, to the extent possible;
      3. Support and increase the availability of apprenticeships in local government, as well as other employment programs in a local government context;
      4. Deliver new capabilities to improve outcomes in housing, planning, emergency management and aged care; and
      5. Ensure the Government publishes an annual summary of funding for Local Government.
 
  1. Write to the Prime Minister and Local Government Minister Catherine King welcoming their commitment to address the crisis in local government financial sustainability and urging them to work with the local government sector to urgently progress the Federation Compact with Local Government.
Carried

  4. agree that officers work alongside OMLS consulting (who has been procured to lodge the application); 
  5. agree that officers request from Crown Lands, a reduced period (of 30 days) for the Acquisition Notice to proceed and an approved Acquisition Notice published in the NSW Government Gazette; and
  6. delegate authority to the Director Community & Development, to finalise the process and this matter, without further report to the Council.
Carried

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"RESOLVED OCM-197-2026 

Moved: Mayor Cornwell McKean
Seconded: Councillor Ngatokoa
That;
  • a submission is prepared for the consultation on ‘The Model Code of Conduct for Council Staff, Delegates and Committee Members – draft for consultation’ (the Draft Code) that:
    1. outlines concerns regarding the applicability of the code to committees formed under section 355 of the Local Government Act 1993 (s355 committees), and
    2. recommends that a separate code consistent with the provisions of S440 of the Local Government Act 1993 and mandatory legal requirements be developed that is specifically applicable to s355 committees identifying their unique role and significant contribution to their local communities
  • a copy of the Draft Code, and accompanying guidance material (such as that provided at https://www.olg.nsw.gov.au/programs-and-initiatives/councillor-conduct-framework-reform), is provided to all section 355 committees.
  • Council delegates finalisation of its submission to the Mayor and CEO given it is due prior to the next council meeting (12 October 2026)
  • Council share copies of its submission with LGNSW and the Country Mayor’s Association
  • A copy of Council’s submission is to be tabled at the October council meeting

Background 
The consultation on the Draft Code provides an opportunity for Council to highlight to the Office of Local Government that the Draft Code is not suitable for volunteer committees of council (s355 committees) and that a separate code should be developed that specifically deals with those committees.
Volunteer committees have a unique role within our community undertaking services that may not be otherwise provided.  While it is recognised that some of the provisions of the Draft Code are required by virtue of legislation, there is a significant bureaucratic overlay in the Draft Code which is impractical and unnecessary for s355 committees.   A simpler, more practical code that recognises that s355 committees are not employees of council and balances mandatory requirements with fit for purpose obligations is a more suitable approach for this particular cohort.
Carried

Volunteer committees have a unique role within our community undertaking services that may not be otherwise provided.  While it is recognised that some of the provisions of the Draft Code are required by virtue of legislation, there is a significant bureaucratic overlay in the Draft Code which is impractical and unnecessary for s355 committees.   A simpler, more practical code that recognises that s355 committees are not employees of council and balances mandatory requirements with fit for purpose obligations is a more suitable approach for this particular cohort."}]},{"id":1647,"name":"MINUTES","parentId":-1,"sortOrder":31,"minutesSortOrder":33,"minutesParentId":-1,"outlineNumber":"","fullOutlineNumber":"","htmlContent":"[IGNORE_INDENT][IGNORE_NUMBERING]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"","isPublic":false,"isPublished":false,"isCurrentItem":false,"meeting":null,"reports":[],"attachments":[],"actionSheets":[],"bookmarks":[],"minutes":[]},{"id":1648,"name":"Confidential Minutes","parentId":1647,"sortOrder":32,"minutesSortOrder":34,"minutesParentId":1647,"outlineNumber":"","fullOutlineNumber":"","htmlContent":"[IGNORE_INDENT][IGNORE_NUMBERING]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"","isPublic":false,"isPublished":false,"isCurrentItem":false,"meeting":null,"reports":[],"attachments":[],"actionSheets":[],"bookmarks":[],"minutes":[]},{"id":1655,"name":"Extension of tenure for ARIC independent member, Todd Bentley ","parentId":1222,"sortOrder":33,"minutesSortOrder":35,"minutesParentId":1222,"outlineNumber":"6.","fullOutlineNumber":"9.6.","htmlContent":"
